Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are out in the middle and the two openers for New Zealand are Fakhar Zaman and Imam-ul-Haq. Tim Southee to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, New Zealand have posted a decent total on the board and with the breeze around, the dew should not be a factor in this chase. They have played Ish Sodhi in this game and he will be key for them if they want to defend this total. Pakistan, on the other hand will feel confident of gunning this total down as their top order is in good form. Will they be able to do it and a take an unassailable lead? Or will the Kiwis fightback and stop them? We will find out in a bit. Stay tuned for the second essay.

Mohammad Nawaz is in for a quick chat. He says that it was turning from the start but the Kiwi batters played well. Adds that he then tried to slow it up and got the wicket of Daryl Mitchell. Says there was bounce on offer as well. Reckons that they can chase down the total easily but the pitch is a bit tricky.

Pakistan showed great character and determination throughout their bowling effort. Naseem Shah gave them the perfect start by getting rid of Allen in the first over. However, after that, they lost their way and allowed the Kiwis to build a huge partnership. Despite bowling well after the Powerplay to keep the runs in check, their spinners were unable to break the stand between Kane Williamson and Devon Conway. They kept trying, but it wasn't happening for them, and they also gave Kane Williamson a couple of lives by dropping him twice in the same over. Their fielding was a bit off as well. It was the 30th over, and Babar Azam gave the ball to Naseem Shah again, who did not let his captain down and knocked over Conway. That turned the game around for them, as Mohammad Nawaz from the other end absolutely ripped through the middle order of the Kiwis. He ended his spell with figures of 10-0-38-4 and was their best bowler. Naseem finished with three scalps, while Usama Mir and Haris Rauf picked up one wicket each. At one point, things were looking bleak for the home side, but they never lost hope and made an excellent comeback against a top side and bowled them out for a total that they will feel is gettable on this wicket. The only concern for them will be their slow-over rate and they will need to improve that in their upcoming games or else it could cost them. It is now up to their batters to maintain their good form and chase down this total in order to win the series.

New Zealand once again failed to impress with their overall batting performance. They did not start well, as they lost Finn Allen in the very first over. After that, Kane Williamson and Devon Conway steadied the ship for a bit. Conway struggled a bit initially, but once both of them got set, it was smooth sailing from there. The spinners restricted the run flow for a bit, but they managed to get through that period. Conway got to his century in no time, but lost his wicket just after that. Both of them added a massive 181 runs for the second wicket. When these two were batting, it looked like the Kiwis would easily cross the 320-run mark. However, after the dismissal of Conway, it went downhill for them as they lost three wickets in nine deliveries, which included the wicket of Kane, who missed out on his hundred by 15 runs. This happened because he kept losing partners at the other end and tried to slow the game down, but was undone by a ripper from Mohammad Nawaz. The Kiwis were 183-1 at one point before falling to 206-6. A gritty knock from Mitchell Santner in the end took them over the 260-run mark, which gives their bowlers something to work with.

A late flurry from the Kiwis and they get to a respectable total. However, we have seen a fine bowling display from Pakistan and they made a good comeback in the middle. It will not going to be an easy chase though and we surely have a game on our hands.

OUT! RUN OUT! Mitchell Santner gets run out looking for two and that concludes the Kiwi innings. This is full and on the stumps, Santner drives it straight long off and turns back for the second straightaway. Mohammad Wasim there picks up the ball and fires the ball towards the keeper. Mohammad Rizwan whips off the bails and even the dive doesn't save Santner. New Zealand finish with 261 on the board!
Well bowled! Slower one, into the pitch and outside off, Mitchell Santner leaves it alone but no wide is called.

Misfield and they get another couple of runs! In the blockhole outside off, Mitchell Santner jams it out straight to backward point where Imam-ul-Haq fumbles badly and allows the batters to take two runs.
This is dug in short and around middle, Mitchell Santner pulls it down to deep mid-wicket and races back for the second. Excellent running!
SIX! BANG! Slower one, full and around leg stump. Mitchell Santner picks it up and clears the front leg before smoking it over the long on fence for a biggie.
Naseem Shah (8-0-47-3) to bowl the last over. However, Pakistan are two-overs behind and will have to keep an extra fielder inside the circle.
Fuller and at the stumps, this is pushed down to long on but they don't take the single.
Shorter and on leg stump, Santner jabs it in front of mid-wicket for one. The 250 is now up for New Zealand.
Back of a length and around middle, Mitchell Santner gets on top of the bounce and pulls it in front of deep mid-wicket. Santner sprints back for the second and puts in the dive to get home safely.
Takes pace off again and bowls it around the top of off, Santner backs away and taps it toward backward point.
WIDE! Another slower one, full and well outside the off stump, left alone for a wide.
FOUR! Slower one, pitched up around middle, Mitchell Santner backs away and lofts it over extra cover for a boundary. Finally, a boundary after 97 deliveries!
Around the top of off and this is bowled from around the wicket. Mitchell Santner punches it straight to cover.
Fullish length on off stump and this one tails back in, Lockie Ferguson blocks it out.
Slower one, very full and on leg stump, Lockie Ferguson drives it straight to mid on.
On a hard length around middle, Lockie Ferguson looks tp push at it but gets an inside edge back on the deck.
WIDE! Pace on this time, on a good length and angling well down the leg side. Wided.
WIDE! An attempted slower one but it is spilled down the leg side for a wide.
This is full and on off stump, Lockie Ferguson drives it toward extra cover.
Lockie Ferguson is the last man in for New Zealand.

OUT! CAUGHT! Straight to the man! Naseem Shah bowls this one short and on the body. Tim Southee swivels a bit and whips it off his hips. The ball is timed well but goes flat and towards deep backward square leg where Usama Mir takes a sharp catch to his right. Shah picks up his third wicket and New Zealand are just one wicket away from being bowled out here.
Commentary.Howout: c Usama Mir b Naseem Shah

Commentary.Commentary: Good length around the top of off, tapped away in front of point for a single.
Very full and on middle, Tim Southee pushes it to the left of the bowler who makes a brilliant tumbling stop on his followthrough.
Naseem Shah (7-0-44-2) comes back into the attack now.
WIDE! This is full and quick, just angling down the leg side. Wided.
Bangs it in short over middle and leg at 142 clicks. Tim Southee ducks under it well.
Good length around off, Tim Southee eases it onto the off side.
Tim Southee walks out to bat now.

OUT! TIMBER! A crackerjack of a delivery from Haris Rauf and Ish Sodhi has to walk back. This is very full and quick, just under 140 clicks and aimed at the base of leg stump. Ish Sodhi backs away a bit looking to dig it out on the off side but is beaten for raw pace. The ball castles into the stumps and Rauf is delighted to get his first wicket of the game.
Nice change up! This is the slower one, on a good length and over off stump. Ish Sodhi gets completely deceived by it and misses the big heave across the line.
Hard length, on a tighter line around off and at 141 clicks. Mitchell Santner nudges it down to third man for one.
This is full and straight, Ish Sodhi backs away but only manages to defend it out.
Risky single! This is full and outside off, Mitchell Santner jams it out towards cover and scampers through for the single. Luckily for him, the fielder missed the direct hit at the bowler's end.
Nails the yorker on leg stump, Ish Sodhi jams it out through mid-wicket for a single.
Full, quick and at the stumps, Ish Sodhi blocks it out.

Edged...but wide of the keeper! This is very full around off and the ball reverses a bit as well. Mitchell Santner looks to drive but gets an outside edge. Mohammad Rizwan springs to his left but can't get to it. They get a single down to third man.
On a hard length around middle, Ish Sodhi backs away and hits it straight to mid on for a quick single.
A slower one again, on a length and on off, Mitchell Santner dabs it towards point.
Back of a length and on middle, Ish Sodhi clips it towards deep square leg for one.
On a length and on off, slower too, Mitchell Santner pushes it towards covers for a single.
Haris Rauf bowls a misdirected short delivery down the leg side, Mitchell Santner leaves it alone. It is called a wide.
Short of a length and outside off, Mitchell Santner steers it through point for a brace.
Back of a length and on middle, Ish Sodhi gets hurried and inside edges it towards the short fine leg region. They cross.
This is on a good length and on middle, Ish Sodhi keeps it out to the leg side.
Haris Rauf (7-0-31-0) is back into the attack.
Goes fuller and on middle, Mitchell Santner knocks it back to the bowler. Three dots in a row to end the over then.
This is on a hard length and outside off, Mitchell Santner looks to punch it away, but misses.
Length again and on middle, Mitchell Santner blocks it towards mid off.
On a length and on off, Ish Sodhi pushes it through covers for a run.
Full and on middle, Mitchell Santner nudges it towards fine leg for a single.
This is on a good length and on middle, Mitchell Santner pushes it towards mid on.
Mohammad Wasim (5-0-40-0) is back on.
Another dot to end the over! This is floated, full and on off, Ish Sodhi fends it to the off side.
Flighted, full and on off, Ish Sodhi drills it towards point.
Quicker, short and on middle, Ish Sodhi only manages to block it to the off side.
Fires this one full and down the leg, Ish Sodhi misses his pull shot. Wided.
Short again and on off, Ish Sodhi dabs it towards point again.
Slightly shorter and on off, Ish Sodhi cuts it towards point.
Tossed up, full and on off, turning away sharply, Ish Sodhi has a poke at it, but gets beaten.
Flighted and around off, Ish Sodhi uses his feet and drives it towards long on for one more.
Flatter, full and on middle, Ish Sodhi works it towards mid-wicket.
Shortish and outside off, Mitchell Santner cuts it towards sweeper cover for one.
Floated, full and on middle, Ish Sodhi eases it towards long on for a single.
A bit short and on off, Mitchell Santner punches it towards sweeper cover for a run.
Tossed up, full and on off, Mitchell Santner goes for the big drive, but misses it completely.
Flatter, short and outside off, Ish Sodhi slashes hard at it, but misses.
Flighted, full and on middle, Ish Sodhi is solid in his defense again.
Looped up, full and on off, Ish Sodhi defends it to the off side.
Ish Sodhi is the new man in.

OUT! LBW! Usama Mir gets a wicket now as Michael Bracewell goes back to the hut. Usama Mir bowls the googly, slower through the air, on middle, turning away, Michael Bracewell looks to play at it, but fails to pick it and misses to get rapped on the pads. There is a huge appeal for LBW, and up goes the finger. Pakistan players are delighted as Ball Tracking shows that wicket's is umpires call. New Zealand seven down now!

Michael Bracewell has been adjudged LBW but he has opted for the review. The third umpire checks UltraEdge first and finds that no bat is involved. Ball Tracking shows the wickets as umpire's call and the onfield decision of Out remains.
Slightly shorter and around leg, Mitchell Santner looks to push it away, but gets an inside edge towards fine leg for a single.
Tossed up, full and on middle, Mitchell Santner leans on and blocks it out.
Powerplay 3! Now, five fielders are allowed outside the circle till the last over. Also, Usama Mir (8-0-40-0) is back into the attack.
A bit flatter and around off, this is punched away through covers for one more.
This is tossed up on off stump, Michael Bracewell drives it through mid off and rotates the strike.
This is very full and on middle and leg, Mitchell Santner punches it down to long on for a single.
Drops it a bit short around off, Michael Bracewell cuts it through cover-point for yet another single.
This is around off, Santner strokes it through covers for one.
WIDE! This is tossed up well outside the off stump. Mitchell Santner leaves it alone for a wide.
This is a bit short and wide, Mitchell Santner cuts it square on the off side for a couple of runs.
Agha Salman (2-0-16-0) comes back into the attack now.
A dot to end a fine spell of bowling from Mohammad Nawaz, he finishes with figures of, 10-0-38-4. This is tossed up outside off, Michael Bracewell defends it off the front foot.

Lucky! This is flighted full and around off stump. Mitchell Santner looks to drive against the turn and gets an inside edge past the stumps. The ball goes through backward square leg and they take one.
Drags the length back and angles it into the pads, Michael Bracewell works it away through mid-wicket for a single.
Tosses it up full and outside off, Mitchell Santner strokes it away to mid off and picks up a quick run.
This is floated up around off, Mitchell Santner drives it toward mid off.
Nicely tossed up well outside off, Mitchell Santner looks to drive off the back foot but gets a big inside edge back onto the pads.
A length ball, drifting onto the pads, this is flicked down to fine leg for a single.
This is pitched up in the channel around off and angling across, Mitchell Santner makes a watchful leave.

A bit of hesitation in the middle but they do get the run. Rauf comes from around the wicket and delivers a short ball around off. Michael Bracewell nudges it to the left of the bowler and they scamper through for one.
Goes a bit fuller at 142.5 clicks and keeps it outside off, Michael Bracewell drives it well but straight to the man at point.
On a hard length and slanted well across the left hander, Michael Bracewell taps it towards backward point.
Good length around the top of off and at 144 clicks, Michael Bracewell solidly blocks it out on the off side.
Flatter one on off stump, Mitchell Santner tentatively blocks it out.
Nagging length around off, Mitchell Santner keeps it out.

This is fired in full and outside off, Mitchell Santner has a little dab at it but the ball zips past the outside edge. There is a stifled appeal for caught behind but the keeper says that he didn't hear anything. Babar Azam doesn't review it though.
Mitchell Santner is the next batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Straight to the man and New Zealand lose their 6th wicket. Mohammad Nawaz bowls this one shorter and a bit quicker at 91.6 clicks. This is around middle and Glenn Phillips hangs back as he looks to slog it away. The ball is hit flat and hard but straight toward deep backward square leg. Fakhar Zaman over there moves a afew inches to his right and takes a siumple catch. Nawaz picks up his fourth and Phillips has to walk back disappointed with himself.
Commentary.Howout: c Fakhar Zaman b Mohammad Nawaz

Commentary.Commentary: Floats it fuller and on the pads, Glenn Phillips keeps it out.
This is slower and shorter, turning into middle, Michael Bracewell pushes it down to long on off the back foot and picks up a single.

Good running! This is fuller and angled across the off stump. Michael Bracewell looks to drive but gets it off the toe end of the bat and the ball bounces back on the deck. Glenn Phillips calls Bracewell for the run and they scamper through with ease.
This is pitched up around the off pole, Michael Bracewell hits it straight toward mid off.
Halt! Aleem Dar, the umpire gets hit on his ankle from the throw on the previous delivery. The physio is in and applying the magic spray. We are ready to continue now.

Good length on the pads at 142 clicks, Glenn Phillips flicks it away behind square on the leg side for a single. The throw from the deep is fired in at the bowler's end and it hits the ankle of the umpire who isn't too pleased about it.
This is shorter and around off, Phillips plays it off the back foot in front of extra cover.
Pacy delivery, pitched up on off stump at 147.4 clicks and Glenn Phillips just about manages to block it out.
Back of a length around off, Michael Bracewell hops and keeps it down in front of point for a quick run.
This is shorter and angling down leg, Michael Bracewell works it off his hips and toward fine leg for a single.
Michael Bracewell walks out to bat now.

OUT! KNOCKED HIM OVER! Mohammad Nawaz with another ripper of a delivery and Kane Williamson has to walk back. Nawaz bowls this at around 89 clicks and drifts it into middle stump. Williamson presses forward to make the block but the ball just pitches and turns away sharply. The ball zips past the outside edge and hits the top of the off stump. Williamson hears the death rattle and he cannot believe it. The skipper departs after a good knock but the Kiwis are now in big trouble here.
Bowls it a bit flatter and outside off, Williamson backs away and taps it toward cover.
Floats it up full and on middle and leg, Williamson pushes it straight to mid on.
This is quicker and fired in around middle, Phillips gets an inside edge toward square leg for a quick run.
Nagging length, angling on the pads, Glenn Phillips goes on the back foot and keeps it out on the leg side.
Well fielded! This is full and around off at almost 143 clicks, Williamson drives it firmly to the left of the bowler. Haris Rauf dives down to that side and makes the stop.
Fullish length, at 140 clicks and at the stumps. Glenn Phillips looks to drive but gets an inside edge toward backward square for a single. The 200 is up for New Zealand now.
Length ball, angling in from outside off at 142 clicks, Williamson drives on the up and plays it toward sweeper cover for a single.
Goes fuller now and angles it into middle and leg at 139.5 clicks. Kane Williamson solidly blocks it out.
Back of a length and outside off, Kane Williamson eases it down in front of point.
On a good length around off, Williamson hangs back and dabs it in front of point.
Glenn Phillips comes out to the middle now. Also, Haris Rauf (4-0-24-0) is back on.

OUT! LBW! Mohammad Nawaz gets his man in the end and Pakistan get two wickets in one over. This is quicker and flatter, turning in sharply from around off. Tom Latham gets pushed on the back foot as he looks to flick it away but misses the ball and gets pinged on the pads. There is another big appeal for lbw and this one seems even closer but the umpire turns it down yet again. Mohammad Nawaz cannot believe it and Babar Azam reviews it. Nothing on UltraEdge and this time Ball Tracking comes up with three reds. Latham has to walk back and Nawaz is absolutely delighted. Pakistan coming back strongly here.
Aerial but safe! Tossed up and turning into the pads, Tom Latham gets down on one knee and paddles it off the top edge behind square leg for a couple of runs.

It seems like Nawaz knew Tom Latham would look to sweep and just holds it back a touch and spins it in from around off. Latham does opt for the sweep but misses and gets a rap on the pads. There is a huge appeal for lbw and Mohammad Nawaz is confident about it. The umpire turns it down but eventually, Babar Azam does review it. The third umpire checks UltraEdge first and there's a flat line as the ball passes the bat. Ball Tracking shows that the ball is just clipping the leg stump and it remains Not Out on umpire's call.
Tom Latham joins his skipper out in the middle now.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! An absolute peach of a delivery from Mohammad Nawaz and Daryl Mitchell cannot believe what just happened here. This is bowled on a shorter length and drifted in from the off stump. Mitchell goes on the back foot and looks to pull out of the punch shot. The ball though grips and turns away taking the outside edge. Mohammad Rizwan takes a sharp catch to his right and Mitchell has to walk back for a low score.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Rizwan b Mohammad Nawaz

Commentary.Commentary: Nicely bowled! This is drifted into middle, Daryl Mitchell looks to come down the track but has to adjust and blocks it out.
Shorter and around off, Kane Williamson backs away and cuts it to deep point for a single.
FOUR! Smart shot! Pitched up around middle, Daryl Mitchell knows that mid on is up and just lofts it over the man there to pick up a boundary.
Just a hint of reverse there. This is pitched and angled in from outside off, Daryl Mitchell blocks it off the front foot.
Hard length around off, Williamson opens the face of the bat late and plays it down to third man for one more.
Good length around off, Daryl Mitchell walks toward the ball and nudges it in front of mid-wicket for a quick single.
Back of a length and outside off, Williamson hangs back and steers it down to third man for a single.

Big confusion between the two batters but no harm is done. This is full and around off, Kane Williamson mistimes the straight drive back to the bowler. The ball deflects off Naseem Shah's hands and goes toward mid on. Williamson hurries down to the other end but Daryl Mitchell sends him back. Thankfully for Williamson, the fielder misses the shy at the striker's end.
Tossed up delivery outside off, Daryl Mitchell strokes it away toward Babar Azam at extra cover.
Floats it up outside off, Daryl Mitchell pushes it off the front foot and towards mid off.
On a length and drifted onto the pads, Williamson flicks it 'round the corner for a single.
This is flatter and around middle,  Williamsontucks it leg side.
FOUR! Lovely stroke! This is full and around off, Williamson plays a lofted checked drive over extra cover and picks up a boundary.
This is a flatter delivery angled into middle and leg, Kane Williamson works it toward mid-wicket.

Drinks break! Just when New Zealand looked to be really pressing on the accelerator, Naseem Shah has provided a big breakthrough for Pakistan. Nevertheless, the 181-run stand between Kane Williamson and Devon Conway has put the Kiwis in a commanding position and with the skipper still out in the middle, they will be targeting a score of above 320 runs. The hosts have the much-needed breakthrough but need to build on this and not let the opposition build another stand. Also, Daryl Mitchell walks out to bat now with Mohammad Nawaz coming back into the attack.

OUT! TIMBER! Naseem Shah strikes! Pakistan gets a crucial wicket and finally breaks this huge partnership. Naseem Shah serves this on a good length and on around middle, shaping away a bit, Devon Conway goes for the drive, but gets beaten by the movement and misses as the ball goes through to rattle the stumps. Naseem Shah once again does the trick for Pakistan and this could be the opening they were looking for. Devon Conway played a fine innings, but has to go back to the hut now. New Zealand two down now!
Back of a length and on off, Devon Conway looks to play at it, but gets an inside edge to te leg side.
Naseem Shah continues with his shorter length, on middle, Kane Williamson forces it towards deep mid-wicket for one.
Short again and on middle, Devon Conway hops and nudges it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Short and around leg, Kane Williamson glances it towards fine leg for a single.
Good bowling! This is on a good length and around off, Kane Williamson looks to play at it, but gets beaten on the outside edge.

HUNDRED FOR CONWAY! This has been an excellent innings from him. He raises his bat and shares a hug with his skipper on the other end. Coming to the delivery, this is darted full and on middle, Devon Conway tucks it towards deep square leg and comes back for the second run. Conway will think about taking the charge now.
Quicker one, full and on middle, Devon Conway this time reverse-sweeps it straight to short third man.

FOUR! Devon Conway is dealing in boundaries now! Usama Mir tosses it up, full and on middle, Devon Conway plays the reverse-sweep with perfection and beats the deep point fielder who puts in a dive to his right but fails to stop it.
Flatter, full and on off, Devon Conway knocks it towards mid-wicket.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Usama Mir floats this up, full and on middle, Devon Conway reverse sweeps it again, but this time over backward point for a boundary.
FOUR! A good start to the over for the Kiwis! This is tossed up, full and on middle, Devon Conway goes for the reverse sweep and nails it towards the deep backward point fence for a boundary.
This is on a hard length and on middle, Kane Williamson blocks it down the pitch.
FOUR! Great stroke! Naseem Shah serves this fuller and on middle, Kane Williamson whips it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Back of a length and on off, Devon Conway punches it through covers for a run.
Length again and on midde, Kane Williamson flicks it through square leg for a single.
This is on a good length and on off, Kane Williamson comes down the track and thrashes it towards backward point where Imam-ul-Haq dives to his right to stop it.
Full and on middle, Kane Williamson clips it towards short mid-wicket.
Naseem Shah (4-0-28-1) is brought back into the attack. Can he break this stand for his team?
Short again and on middle, Devon Conway moves back and tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Short and on off, Kane Williamson cuts it towards sweeper cover for a run.
A googly now, full and on middle, turning away, Devon Conway dabs it towards short third man for a quick single.
Flatter, full and on leg, Devon Conway works it towards mid-wicket.
Floated, full and on off, Kane Williamson uses his feet and eases it towards long off for a single.
Nicely tossed up, short and on off, turning away sharply, Kane Williamson gets beaten on the outside edge.
FOUR! A gift from Mohammad Wasim! He bowls a juicy full toss, on off, Devon Conway shows the full face of the bat and drives it well past mid off for a boundary.
Short of a length and on middle, Devon Conway clips it past mid-wicket for a couple of runs. The 150-run partnership also comes up with that.
Back of a length and on off, Kane Williamson guides it towards third man for a run.
A slower one now, on a length and on off, Kane Williamson taps it towards point.
Full but down the leg, Kane Williamson misses his flick. Wided. 150 up for New Zealand!
On a length and on middle, Devon Conway flicks it through square leg for a single.

SIX! BANG! Devon Conway hits the first maximum of the match! Mohammad Wasim bowls this a touch fuller and outside off, Devon Conway skips down the track and slices it, but the breeze takes the ball over the deep point fence for a biggie.
Shortish again and on off, Devon Conway moves back and punches it towards long on for one.
Shorter in length and outside off, Kane Williamson cuts it towards deep point for a run.
Slower through the air, on off, turning away, Kane Williamson taps it towards covers.
A low full toss, on off, Kane Williamson digs it back to the bowler.
Floated, full and on off, Kane Williamson pushes it towards covers where the fielder dives to his right to stop it.
Tossed up, full and on off, Kane Williamson drives it wide of deep point for a brace.
Usama Mir (5-0-19-0) is back into the attack.
Short again and on off, Devon Conway forces it towards mid-wicket.
Short of a length and on middle, Devon Conway only manages to push it back to the bowler.
Back of a length and on off, Kane Williamson steers it towards third man for one more.
Mohammad Wasim bangs in a bouncer, on middle, Devon Conway pulls it towards deep square leg for one.

Overthrows! This is on a good length and on off, Kane Williamson taps it towards point and calls for the run, but he is sent back. The fielder misses his shy at the batter's end and the ball goes towards deep square leg. Now, the batters take the run.

FOUR! Kane Williamson finds the fence this time. This is short and on middle, Kane Williamson slaps it, but does not get the timing right. However, the ball is in the gap between mid-wicket and mid on and races away towards the wide long on fence for a boundary.
Quicker one, short and on middle, Devon Conway moves back and plays it towards extra covers.
Shorter in length and outside off, Devon Conway cuts it towards sweeper cover for a brace.
Looped up and on off, Kane Williamson pushes it towards covers for a quick single.
Flatter, full and on middle, Devon Conway reverse sweeps it towards third man for a run.
FOUR! Good shot! This is floated, full and on off, Devon Conway uses his feet, goes inside out and lofts it over extra covers for a boundary.
Tossed up, full and on middle, Kane Williamson drives it towards long on for a single.
Back of a length and on off, Kane Williamson guides it towards third man for a single.

DROPPED AGAIN! Kane Williamson is living a charmed life here. This is on a hard length and down the leg, Kane Williamson tries for the pull shot, but the ball just brushes off his gloves and goes towards the keeper. Mohammad Rizwan there dives to his left, but fails to pouch it. Pakistan need to up their fieldng here.
On a length and on middle, Kane Williamson knocks it towards mid on.
Short of a length and on off, Devon Conway cuts it towards sweeper cover for a run.

DROPPED! Haris Sohail is the culprit here! Mohammad Wasim lands this short and on middle, Kane Williamson pulls it aerially towards short mid-wicket where Haris Sohail flies to his right, gets both hands but spills it. A single is taken. This could prove to be a costly miss for Pakistan.
Back of a length and on off, Kane Williamson pushes it towards short covers.
Flighted delivery and around middle, Kane Williamson uses his feet again and chips it down to long on for one.
Looped up, full and on off, Devon Conway leans on and taps it towards covers for a run.
Quicker one, full and on middle, Devon Conway tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Tossed up, full and on middle, turning away, Devon Conway goes for the sweep again, but misses and gets hit on the pads as the ball rolls to the off side.
FOUR! Great shot! This is floated, full and on middle, Devon Conway goes down and nails his sweep it towards the deep square leg fence for a boundary.
Agha Salman begins with a flatter delivery, full and on off, Kane Williamson uses his feet and drills it towards mid off and scampers across for a single.
Agha Salman is now brought into the attack.
FOUR! Lovely timing! Good length around middle, Devon Conway plays a beautiful straight drive off the back foot and beats Fakhar Zaman at mid off who dives to his left. The ball races into the fence.
Pitches it up now around off, Devon Conway tentatively drives it straight towards mid off.
WIDE! Tries to go fuller and attack the pads but ends up spilling it down the leg side.
On a hard length around middle at 144.3 clicks, Devon Conway manages to keep it out on the leg side.
Bowls it a touch fuller on middle and leg, Conway punches it out to mid on.
Easy two! Good length on the pads, Conway tucks it away to the right of the man at fine leg and picks up a couple of runs.
Back of a length and outside off, Kane Williamson hops and slaps it down to sweeper cover for a single.
Mohammad Wasim replaces Mohammad Nawaz. He conceded seven runs in his first over.

FOUR! Up and over and Devon Conway gets to his 3rd ODI FIFTY in style! Tossed up around off, Conway steps out and goes inside-out over extra cover to find the fence. The 100-run partnership is up between these two and Conway will now look to play a bit more freely.

That will be FIFTY for Kane Williamson and he has got to his 41st ODI half-century without breaking a sweat. This is flatter and outside off, Williamson taps it through covers for a single. The 100 also comes up for New Zealand and Williamson will look to convert this into a big one now.
Tosses it up now, full and outside off. Devon Conway looks to go over extra cover but drives it square on the off side for a single.
Pulls the length back a touch and bowls it around off, Conway keeps it out on the off side.
Williamson looks for two but has to settle for a single. This is flighted, on a length and outside off. Williamson drives it down to long off for a run.
Usama Mir changes his angle and comes from around the wicket. This is full and angling down leg, Conway sweeps it down to fine leg and gets off strike.

Sloppy fielding from the skipper! This is tossed up on leg stump, Devon Conway flicks it straight to Babar Azam at short mid-wicket who just lets it slip through his hands. They pick up a single as well.
Floated up on middle and leg, Williamson knocks it down to long on and collects a run.
Well bowled! Holds it back a touch and drifts it onto middle, Williamson blocks it off the front foot.
Full and on leg stump, Devon Conway gets inside the line of the ball and paddles it 'round the corner for a run.
Nicely flighted, full and on the stumps, this is worked away in front of mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! This is a real drag down by Mohammad Nawaz outside off. Kane Williamson has to reach for it but manages to pull it into the mid-wicket fence for a boundary.
This is floated up on the pads, Devon Conway flicks it towards short fine leg. Five dots in a row to end the over and only 2 runs come off it.
And again! In the blockhole around middle and Conway goes too hard at it only managing to mistime it back to the bowler.
Very full and on middle, Devon Conway looks to hit it hard back past the bowler but mistimes it badly.
Keeps it full and around off, Conway defends it out. Conway has been bogged down a bit by the spinners after a quick start and seems to be struggling here.
Well struck but straight to the man! This is very full around off, Devon Conway plays a thumping drive but straight to the fielder at short cover.
This is tossed up full and around middle, Devon Conway whips it in between mid-wicket and mid on and picks up a couple of runs.
This is fuller and on leg stump, Devon Conway flicks it a bit uppishly and past the man at mid-wicket for a single.
Devon Conway looks to come down the pitch and Mohammad Nawaz sees him coming. Nawaz drags the length back considerably and bowls it on the pads. Conway can only manage to block it out.
Floats it up full and on middle, Kane Williamson drives it down to long on and rotates the strike.
Slightly fuller and on middle, Conway works it through wide mid on for a single.
Pulls the length back and bowls it around the pads, Devon Conway looks to use his feet but has to adjust and ends up just tucking it toward mid-wicket.
Flatter delivery around middle, Conway plays it off the back foot but straight to silly mid on.

Drinks! After losing an early wicket, New Zealand are going steadily with both Kane Williamson and Devon Conway set. However, the spinners of Pakistan have managed to restrict the run flow, but they would like to break this stand quickly.  Mohammad Nawaz to continue after the break.

A dot to end and only a single comes off it, the scoring rate just dropping down here for New Zealand. This is the quicker one, drifted in full and on middle and leg. Williamson blocks it off the front foot.
This is dragged down slightly and bowled on off stump, Kane Williamson taps it in front of cover-point.
Floated up on middle and leg, Devon Conway drives it down to long on for one.
This is pushed through quicker and on leg stump, Conway flicks it toward square leg.
Tossed up on a nagging length around off, Devon Conway looks to play the lofted drive but mistimes it along the ground toward mid off.
Shorter one around off, this one stays a touch low and Devon Conway pushes it back to the bowler.
Devon Conway sets up for the paddle but Nawaz fires it in full and on leg stump. Conway manages to get some bat on it and get it behind square leg for a run.
Around middle and leg, this is worked away in front of mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted delivery outside off, Kane Williamson presses forward and pushes it toward extra cover.
Leg bye! Flatter one down leg, Devon Conway looks to tuck it away but the ball goes off his pads toward short fine leg. They get a leg bye.
A tad shorter and around off, Devon Conway punches it out.
Cheeky attempt! This is flatter and angled into the pads, Devon Conway looks for the reverse sweep but misses. The ball flicks his hips before the keeper collects it.
Flatter one around off, Devon Conway looks to cut it hard but only gets the ball to deep point for a single.
Quicker and flatter, close to the off pole, Williamson dabs it down to short third man and scampers through for one.
This is a tad shorter and outside off, Conway cuts it to deep cover-point for yet another single.
Nicely tossed up around off, Kane Williamson drives it off the front foot down to long off for a single.
This is down the leg side, Devon Conway paddles it uppishly down to fine leg and picks up a single.
This is fired in full and on the pads, Devon Conway nudges it on the leg side.

FOUR! Excellent placement from Williamson! This is a fraction shorter on middle, Williamson hops on the back foot and wrists it well in front of mid-wicket. Naseem Shah from long on tries to run around but his sliding effort isn't enough to stop the boundary.
Slower through the air and a bit flatter, drifted onto the pads. This one stays a touch low as Devon Conway works it through mid-wicket for a single.
This is fuller on middle and leg, Williamson knocks it down to long on for a single.
Nicely flighted, on off stump and Kane Williamson reaches forward to block.
This is around middle and leg, Devon Conway turns it through mid-wicket for a run.
Flighted, on a length and around off, Williamson pushes it through extra cover and rotates the strike.
This is on a length and around middle, Devon Conway defends it out.

NOT OUT! Pakistan cannot believe it but in the end, it is a wasted review. Usama Mir tosses it up on a length around off stump and the ball spins back in. Devon Conway strides forward to defend but seems to have missed it. The ball pings into the front pad and there is a big appeal. The umpire turns it down and it is reviewed. The third umpire checks UltraEdge and finds that the ball hit the bat and pad simultaneously and hence, stays with the onfield call. However, the replays also shows that after hitting the bat, it goes towards the keeper, but Mohammad Rizwan behind the stumps was busy appealing for the LBW, and did not attempt for the catch. So, it is a dropped chance as well.

Is that out? Pakistan have taken a review for a LBW appeal. This looks close as the bat is very close to the pads of Devon Conway. The third umpire thinks that it has hit the bat first and stays with the onfield call.
Flighted delivery, full and outside off, Williamson drives it through the cover region and turns the strike over.
Nicely tossed up on off stump, Kane Williamson leans forward to make the block.
This is very full on the pads, Devon Conway clips it past square leg and picks up a single.
Starts off with a shorter one outside off, Kane Williamson waits on the back foot and eases it to deep cover for a single.
Powerplay 2! The fielding side can now have as many as four fielders patrolling the boundary till the 40th over. Also, Usama Mir to have a bowl now.
Flighted delivery, short and on off, Devon Conway leans on and keeps it out.
Quicker one, full and on middle, Devon Conway tucks it towards mid-wicket.
A bit short and on off, Kane Williamson punches it towards long off for a run.
Tossed up, full and on middle, Kane Williamson blocks it out.

DROPPED! A tough chance though! This is floated, short and on middle, sticks to the surface a bit, Devon Conway looks to push it away, but it goes uppishly towards the bowler where Mohammad Nawaz dives to his left, but only manages to get his left hand to it as the ball goes towards long on. They cross.
Mohammad Nawaz starts with a flatter delivery, short and on middle, angling in, Kane Williamson looks to block it, but gets an inside edge towards square leg for a single.
Mohammad Nawaz is now brought into the attack.
Full and off, Devon Conway drives it down the pitch where Kane Williamson does well to get out the way of it. Babar Azam from mid off chases it and dives to keep it inside. Two runs taken!
On a length and on off, Kane Williamson opens the face of the bat and steers it through backward point for a run.
Full and on middle, Kane Williamson defends it back towards the bowler.
Short and outside off, Devon Conway cuts it towards deep point for a single.
Nearly for Haris Rauf! He bowls this back of a length and on off, Devon Conway looks to dab it away, but gets an bottome edge just past the stumps towards the keeper.
This is full and on off, Devon Conway drives it through covers and the fielder from mid off chases and mops it up. The batters comes back for the second run.
Haris Rauf (3-0-18-0) is back on from the opposite end.
Full and on the pads, Kane Williamson nudges it wide of deep square leg where the fielder covers his ground well and slides to his right to stop it. Two runs taken!
Back of a length and on off, Kane Williamson punches it towards covers.

FOUR! Fine shot! Mohammad Wasim bowls this back of a length and on middle, Kane Williamson gets on top of it and wristily flicks it wide of mid-wicket for a boundary. With that, the 50-run partnership comes up between these two batters.
This is a tad fuller and on middle, Kane Williamson tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Short and outside off, Kane Williamson cuts it hard but finds the cover-point fielder.
On a length and on off, Kane Williamson pushes it towards mid off of the back foot.
Mohammad Wasim loses his line and starts with a good-length delivery, way outside off, Kane Williamson leaves it alone. Wided.
Mohammad Wasim comes into the attack now.
FOUR! Devon Conway with the third boundary of the over! This slightly full and around leg, Devon Conway whips it towards the deep mid-wicket fence for four more runs. 13 runs off the over!
Pitched up, on middle, Devon Conway pushes it towards mid on.

FOUR! Two in a row! This is the best shot so far in this innings! Naseem Shah again serves this fuller and on middle, Devon Conway stays there and drives it down the ground towards the long off fence for a boundary.
FOUR! Devon Conway finds the gap! This is overpitched and around leg, Devon Conway flicks it with soft hands wide of mid-wicket and the ball races towards the deep mid-wicket fence for a boundary.
Short of a length and on middle, Kane Williamson taps it in front of mid on for a single.
Fuller one and on middle, Kane Williamson mistimes his drive towards mid on.
Another good-length delivery, on off, Kane Williamson looks to defend it, but gets a thick outside edge towards third man for a run. This has been a steady start for New Zealand!
On a length and on middle, Kane Williamson pushes it back towards the bowler.
Full and on middle, Kane Williamson blocks it down the pitch.
Back of a length and just outside off, Kane Williamson thinks about poking at it, but takes his bat away at the last moment.
FOUR! Nice timing! Haris Rauf bowls this on a hard length and on middle, shaping in, Kane Williamson clips it away towards the deep square leg fence for a boundary.
This is on a good length and around leg, Devon Conway flicks it towards fine leg for a single.

FOUR! Lovely shot! This is the third over in a row that the last ball has gone for a boundary. Naseem Shah bowls this full and around off, Kane Williamson stays there and drives it beautifully through covers for a boundary.
Pitched up, on middle, Kane Williamson knocks it towards short mid-wicket.
Naseem Shah serves this on a hard length and around off, Kane Williamson shoudlers arms to it.
Fuller in length and on off, Kane Williamson drives it towards covers where the fielder lets it through. Two runs taken!
This is on a good length and in the channel outside off, Kane Williamson offers no shot at it.
Full and on off, Kane Williamson drills it towards mid off.

FOUR! Devon Conway finally connects well! Haris Rauf lands this short and on middle, Devon Conway picks up the length early and pulls it on the front foot towards the deep square leg fence for a boundary.
Overpitched and on off, Devon Conway looks to drive, but loses his grip of the and mistimes it towards mid off.
On a length and around off, angling away, keeps low too, Devon Conway leaves it alone.
Goes fuller this time, on middle, Devon Conway tries to drive it away, but again gets an inside edge through square leg and comes back for the second. He is struggling to time the ball here.
Back of a length and off, Devon Conway fends it towards short covers.
This is on a good length and on off, shaping in a bit, Devon Conway looks to block it out, but gets an inside edge towards square leg.
FOUR! Nice shot! Naseem Shah bowls a half-volley, on the leg stump line, Kane Williamson uses his wrists and just clips it wide of mid on for a boundary.
Length again and on off, Kane Williamson steers it towards short third man and denies the run. Four dots now!
Three dots in a row! This is short of a length and on off, Kane Williamson taps it to the off side.
On a length and on off, Kane Williamson leans on and defends it towards short covers.
Full again and on middle, Kane Williamson works it towards mid on.
FOUR! Up and over! Naseem Shah bowls this full and slighty wide of off, Kane Williamson accepts the width and smashes it over backward point for a boundary.
Back of a length and around off, Kane Williamson guides it towards third man for a run and gets off the mark.
Full and on off, shaping in, Kane Williamson knocks it back towards the bowler.
On a length and on middle, Devon Conway tucks it towards wide of mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! That is the first boundary of the innings! Haris Rauf pulls his length back a bit, on off, Devon Conway gently pushes it, but the timing is so good that it beats the cover-point fielder and races away to the fence.
Goes fuller this time, on off, Devon Conway blocks it down the pitch.
Haris Rauf begins with a good-length delivery, on middle, Devon Conway works it with the inner half towards square leg.
Haris Rauf to steam in from the opposite end.
BEAUTY! This is on a hard length and on the fifth stump line, holds its line after hitting the deck, Kane Williamson gets squared up and the ball just goes past the outside edge to the keeper.
Kane Williamson is in early at number 3.

OUT! TAKEN! Naseem Shah draws first blood! Pakistan get the breakthrough in the first over again. Naseem Shah serves this fuller and around off, Finn Allen stays there and drives it uppishly towards short covers where Mohammad Nawaz dives to his left to take a terrific catch. Finn Allen goes back to the hut for a low score and the Kiwis lose their first wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Nawaz b Naseem Shah

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on middle, shaping away, Devon Conway looks to work it away, but gets beaten by the extra bounce and the ball goes off his thigh pads past slip cordon. A single is taken.

Finn Allen gets a bit lucky there! New Zealand get underway in streaky fashion! Naseem Shah once again bowls this on a good length and on off, shaping in, Finn Allen looks to cut it, but gets an inside edge just past the stumps and towards fine leg. They cross.
This is on a good length and around off, Finn Allen lifts his bat and lets it go to the keeper.
Naseem Shah starts with a full delivery, on the pads, swinging in, Finn Allen flicks it towards square leg.

We are all set for the start of the play! The umpires are in the middle and so are the players of Pakistan. Finn Allen and Devon Conway are out in the middle to open the innings for New Zealand and they are wearing black armbands in order to pay respect to former Test cricketer Bruce Murray who recently passed away. Naseem Shah has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Chris Harris is pitchside. He says that there is no grass so it will be a good pitch for batting. Adds that the moisture will come in the second innings and the spinners will play a big part while the pacers will find it a bit difficult.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Devon Conway, Finn Allen, Kane Williamson (C), Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham (WK), Glenn Phillips, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner, Ish Sodhi (In for Henry Shipley), Tim Southee and Lockie Ferguson.
Pakistan (Unchanged XI) - Fakhar Zaman, Imam-ul-Haq, Babar Azam (C), Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Haris Sohail, Agha Salman, Mohammad Nawaz, Mohammad Wasim, Usama Mir, Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf.
TOSS - New Zealand have won the toss and they will BAT first.

New Zealand will be a tad bit disappointed with their performance in the first game but the difference in conditions during the afternoon and in the evening did play a huge role in the outcome of the game. They will look to change the fact that almost all of their batters got a start but no one was able to score big. Michael Bracewell put in a good all-round performance for them but the Kiwis need their pacers to fire. In a do-or-die game, will New Zealand step up and level the series? Or will Pakistan continue on their merry way? We shall find out together. Toss and team news in a bit.

Pakistan made good use of the conditions after winning the toss as Naseem Shah ripped through the Kiwi batting lineup and picked up a memorable five-fer. The bowling performance was on point as whenever a partnership was building they were able to pick up a wicket. As for their batting, three out of the top four batters scored a half-century which allowed them to gun down the total without much fuss. They will now look for consistency and try to win the series in this match itself.

Hello and a warm welcome to all. It is now time for the 2nd ODI between Pakistan and New Zealand from the National Stadium in Karachi once again. The hosts have a 1-0 lead in the three-game series and a win here could prove to be decisive. As for the Kiwis, it is a must-win game if they are to take the series into the decider.
... MATCH DAY ...

The festival of cricket in Pakistan continues as we head towards the second ODI of the three-match series between Pakistan and New Zealand, which will be played at the same venue as the first game, i.e., the National Stadium Karachi. The home fans got something to celebrate as Pakistan won the first ODI quite comfortably in the end, making it nine consecutive wins in this format. This was by far their best performance after a couple of disappointing Test series at home. The duo of Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan were back to their usual bests in scoring half-centuries, while Fakhar Zaman also got some runs under his belt. However, the match was set up by the five-wicket haul from Naseem Shah in the first innings. They were better than the Kiwis in every department. After this win, Pakistan moved into second place in the ICC Super League standings, pushing New Zealand down to third place. The Men in Green will look to continue the momentum and seal the series with one game to spare. New Zealand, on the other hand, were outplayed by Pakistan. No one would have thought that, as the Kiwis are a really dangerous side in this format. Their batting was a bit lackluster, as most of their batters got good starts but no one could convert them into a big score. Talking about their bowling, it wasn't that good either, but they also did not have that many runs on the board considering the wicket. Michael Bracewell has been their best all-rounder for quite a while now, and he performed like that in the first match too. However, Tim Southee and Lockie Ferguson need to use their experience and take more responsibility to handle their bowling attack. They also gave a debut to Henry Shipley in the previous game who can come handy with his all-round abilities. The Kiwis could make a couple of changes as they are in a do-or-die situation to keep their series alive. The weather is expected to be warm, but there will be humidity. Also, the pitch will be good for batting, but the pacers will get help up front and spinners can also get some turn as the game goes deep. We know that New Zealand will never go down without a fight, and we can expect a strong response from them. Will they be able to comeback and level the series? Or will Pakistan wrap up the series? We will find out soon.
